independent_findings.finding: Remove unlinks parent/platform first; platform removal can invoke owner's callback before global cleanup. Global OnRemoveEntity precedes onremove, removes Ents only for a present GUID, and has no finally protection.

Global cleanup deregisters Brain/SG managers and GUID coroutine tasks; this is distinct from the later pendingtasks cancellation. SG removal clears buffered events, but neither manager removal universally calls business Stop or clears entity fields.

onremove snapshots listeners and may still call the current Brain directly even though managers were deregistered. Errors or nested Remove are not isolated; no local validity/idempotence/reentry guard exists in Remove.

Later cleanup order is worldstate, bilateral events, pendingtasks, component OnRemoveEntity, raw replica OnRemoveEntity, update tables, child Remove, platform follower Lua links, entity-specific hook, persists=false, Retire. pairs order within component/replica/child loops is unspecified; mutations are not protected by snapshots.

Remove does not call RemoveComponent for every component, does not clear component slots or use public replica tag access, and does not promise cleanup of arbitrary external-host tasks or resources. A later cleanup hook can create new registrations after the one-time clearing stage; native Retire effects remain unknown.

Conditional static counter observation: when Ents[GUID] and UpdatingEnts[GUID] exist and self.updatecomponents remains truthy, global cleanup decrements num_updating_ents and the later Remove update block decrements it again. This is not a runtime fault verdict or an instruction to patch game code.
RemoveEntity(guid) has a missing-GUID no-op and delayclientdespawn branch; direct EntityScript:Remove has neither guard. Do not transfer the global caller's guards into the instance method contract.

deduplication.incremental_scope: New card owns the whole Remove entry and global cleanup dependencies, prefix/suffix ownership, exception/reentry and native boundary. Existing subscription, event dispatch, replica visibility, RemoveComponent and Periodic contracts remain dependencies with their original Scope/HOLD; do not rebrand them as new findings.
